clips.text_en_c1: Electrical engineer here, with roughly 11 years of professional experience. I design products that actually work, and I genuinely love what I do. Nevertheless, I have repeatedly been laid off or fired for reasons that seem remarkably trivial. The most recent dismissal followed a spelling error, which came after a performance-improvement plan and blame for coordinating different charge hours across several managers. Because I started life at a considerable disadvantage, these setbacks have affected my career far more severely than they might have affected someone with more security or support.
clips.text_en_c2: Electrical engineer here, with roughly eleven years of professional experience. I design products that actually work, and I genuinely love what I do. And yet, with tiresome regularity, I keep being laid off or fired for reasons that border on the absurd. Most recently, the dismissal followed a spelling error, which came after a performance improvement plan and blame for coordinating work involving different charge hours across several superiors. None of this reflects any deficiency in my craft; rather, it reflects how corporate politics can eclipse technical competence. I started life at a considerable disadvantage, and corporate decision-making has done little to narrow that gap.

clips.text_en_c2: Cisco president Jeet Patel reportedly ordered the company’s entire codebase to be replaced with AI-generated code within two years, a sweeping mandate that places artificial intelligence at the heart of corporate survival strategy. Employees are to be granted unrestricted access to AI tokens, with the initial emphasis squarely on rewriting legacy systems. If implemented faithfully, this initiative could reshape entry-level engineering roles, as junior positions traditionally designed to cultivate fundamental skills may disappear altogether; even senior engineers may find themselves perpetually producing and reviewing machine-generated slop. As the original post rightly observes, nobody has yet explained who will be answerable when the legacy code inevitably deteriorates. The thread, notably, offers no investment setup.

clips.text_en_c1: WHITEPILL THREAD: Hot cocoa is the finest pre-workout drink, and virtually anyone can begin lifting without any prior sporting experience. clips.text_en_c2: WHITEPILL THREAD: Hot cocoa is the finest pre-workout ritual, though enthusiasm is no substitute for consistency. Anyone can begin lifting, and prior sporting experience is by no means a prerequisite. With sensible training and adequate nutrition, it is entirely possible to escape skinnyfat mode in under six months, while people typically notice visible progress in your lifting within a year. Beginner programming is refreshingly straightforward, and dietary advice reduces to eating sufficient protein while steering clear of fast food, candy, and soda. A gym membership is helpful, certainly, but not indispensable; anyone can build a decent physique with bodyweight exercises, discipline, and enough time to recover.
